newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska cattle group plans labeled beef program.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska cattle group plans labeled beef program.

text.p: Cattle producers in Nebraska are initiating a program to certify cattle as corn-fed in hopes of increasing consumer demand for beef from their state.

A task force of the Nebraska Cattlemen's association have penned the "Nebraska Corn-Fed Beef", (NCFB), name for the group's program to certify cattle as meeting higher quality standards and as fed a corn-based diet, a release stated.
The goal of the program is to develop a winning combination for consumers and cattle producers, in which consumers receive consistently high quality beef and producers are rewarded for supplying it.

"The NCFB program will build Nebraska's reputation by certifying that product marketed through this program meets strict quality standards," said Nebraska Cattlemen president Dave Bruntz, in the release.

The process includes NCFB's identification of source-verified cattle to be marketed under the program. Calves born after January 1, 1997 will be the first eligible for the program, with beef to be available to consumers late next year.
Mike Fitzgerald, spokesman for Nebraska Cattlemen, told Reuters the association is in the process of seeking approval from the U.S. Agriculture Department for its labeling program.
"We're in the process of preparing applications and we will be meeting with (USDA) next month in Washington D.C.," Fitzgerald said.
